chapter_title: Concerning the Five Storehouses that have poured forth from the Land of Darkness since the [Beginning]; the Five Rulers, the Five Spirits, the Five Bodies, the Five Tastes.
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is dominant in the first two-thirds of this chapter: a systematic five-fold cosmological description of the Kingdom of Darkness, mapping storehouses→elements→trees→genera→worlds, then describing the King of Darkness through zoomorphic forms (lion/eagle/dragon/fish), five properties (darkness/putridity/ugliness/bitterness/burning), three faculties (hardness/magic arts/polyglot knowledge), and further properties (movement/terrifying voice/perceptual limitation). The five sub-king descriptions (¶12-16) each contain pristine substrate (zoomorphic face + metal correspondence + taste correspondence) followed by editorial bridge material applying the cosmic spirit to contemporary institutions ('reigns today in the principalities,' 'sects that worship fire,' 'sites of idols,' 'baptism of the waters,' 'soothsayers'). The editorial fatigue pattern is textbook: +10.29 editorial_bridge drift in the second half. Gardner notes textual development and redactorial confusion about the King of Darkness vs. King of Smoke hierarchy. The substrate's five-fold degree structure (Smoke/Fire/Wind/Water/Darkness → gold/copper/iron/silver/lead → salty/sour/sharp/sweet/bitter → lion/eagle/fish/dragon) is a quintessential correspondential map with both sides internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic attribution: 'Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples.' No cosmological content. Standard dialogue frame opener.

paragraphs.core_text: Five storehouses have arisen since the beginning in the land of darkness! The five elements poured out of them. Also, from the five elements were fashioned the five trees! Again, from the five trees were fashioned the five genera of creatures in each world, male and female. And the five worlds themselves have five kings therein, and five spirits, five bodies, five tastes; in each world, they not resembling one another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic emanation hierarchy: storehouses→elements→trees→genera→worlds. Purely systematic, both sides of every mapping internal to the cosmic system. The five-fold pentadic structure is the skeleton of the entire chapter. High substrate score (56.34) confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: The King of the world of Smoke [ ... ] who came up from the depth of darkness; this is he who is the head of all wickedness, and all malignity. The beginning of the spread of the war occured through him; all the battles, fights, quarrelling, dangers, destructions, fights, wrestling-contests! That is the one who first made arise danger and war, with his worlds and his powers. Afterwards, also, he waged war with the light. He pitched a battle with the exalted kingdom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the King of Smoke's cosmic role as originator of the primordial war. Both sides remain within the cosmic system — 'the exalted kingdom' is the Light realm, not a contemporary institution. Gardner notes redactorial confusion about the King of Smoke vs. supreme King of Darkness hierarchy, but the description itself is internal cosmological narrative.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, regarding the King of Darkness, there are five shapes on him! His head is lion-faced; his hands and feet are demon- and devil-faced; his shoulders are eagle-faced; while his belly is dragon-faced; his tail is fish-faced. These five shapes, the marks of his five worlds, exist on the King of the realms of Darkness!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Quintessential zoomorphic-realm mapping: body parts→animal faces→five worlds. This is the correspondential substrate at its purest. The five shapes ARE the marks of five worlds — domain mapped onto domain. The institutional score (5.36) is a false positive from 'demon- and devil-faced' vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, there are five other properties in him. The first is his darkness. The second is his putridity. The third is his ugliness. The fourth is his bitterness, his own soul. The fifth is his burning, which burns like an iron () as if poured out from fire.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Five-fold enumeration of the King's properties. Systematic, impersonal, enumerated teaching. Enumeration markers ('The first is...', 'The second is...') are structural bones of the substrate. Both sides internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: [There are] also three others in him! The first, that his body is hard and very tough, even as she has formed him [ ... ] cruel-hearted; namely Matter, who is the thought of death, [the o]ne who sculpted him from the nature of the land of darkness. This is the manner of the body of the ruler of Smoke. He is harder than every iron, copper and steel and lead; as there is no cleaver at all, nor any iron implement, can [ ... ] him and cut him. For Matter, his fashioner, has formed him [ ... ] strong and hard.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of three faculties. Introduces Matter as personified cosmic fashioner — internal to the cosmic system. Metal comparisons (iron, copper, steel, lead) function as hardness analogies within the correspondential register. Gardner notes the unclear relationship of the supreme King to personified Matter; this passage positions Matter as prior to and fashioner of the King.

paragraphs.core_text: The second, that he wounds and kills by the word of his magic arts. His recitation and hearing, all his foolish instruction, make magic and invocations for him. When it pleases him, he can make an invocation over himself, and by his magic arts be hidden from his companions. Again, when it pleases him, he can be manifested over his powers and appear to them
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'so that these enchantments nowadays, which people utilise (?) [...] this world, are the mysteries of the King of Darkness' — 'nowadays' and 'this world' explicitly anchor to the editorial present. Removed exhortation: 'Concerning this, I command you all the time: Keep away from the magic arts and enchantments of darkness!' and the judgment passage that follows — direct audience address ('I command you'), imperative moral instruction, eschatological threat. The pivot from substrate to editorial occurs at 'so that these enchantments nowadays.'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear mid-paragraph layer boundary. The substrate describes the King's second faculty (magic arts, self-concealment, self-manifestation) — both sides internal. Then 'nowadays' explicitly crosses into the editorial present, followed by first-person exhortation. The editorial_bridge score (8.9) and exhortation score (4.19) correctly flag the later material.

paragraphs.core_text: The third, that the King of the realms of Darkness knows the converse and language of his five worlds. He understands every thing he hears from their mouths, as they address one another; each one of them in his language. [Every] design they will consider against him, every snare they debate with one another to bring upon him, he knows them! He can also understand the gesturing they signal between one another. Yet, his powers and his rulers, who are subject to him, can not understand his wordy converse. While all these things are unveiled to him; still, their heart is not manifested to him. He knows not their mind nor their thought; he can not ponder their beginning and their end. Rather, he only knows and apprehends what is before his eyes.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third faculty: polyglot knowledge but limited perception. Entirely internal to the cosmic system — describes what the King CAN and CANNOT know. The dialectic of power and limitation (knows languages but not hearts, sees what is before his eyes only) is systematic cosmological-correspondential description. The institutional score (2.24) appears to be noise.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, another different thing is found in the King of the realms of Darkness! For when it pleases him to move, he spreads all his limbs out and walks. When it comes to mind, he with[d]raws his limbs and takes them in, and is rolled (?) to his companions; and he falls to the ground like a grape and a great iron ball! He terrifies by his cry, he is frightful. He frightens his powers with his sound; because when he speaks, being like thunder in the clouds, he resembles the [ ... ] of the rocks [ ... ] When he cries out and [ ... ] and calls [ ... ] over his powers, they shall tremble and to[tter a]nd fall under foot; even as some birds would be [ ... ] the bird [ ... / ... ] and they fall down to the earth. Still, this thing only: he knows not what is far from him, he sees not who is at a distance, nor does he hear him. Rather, whoever is before his face he sees, hearing him and knowing him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Additional properties: movement (extension/contraction of limbs), terrifying voice (thunder analogy), and perceptual limitation (repeated from ¶8 — sees only what is before his face). Heavy lacunae but the substrate voice is unmistakable. Similes (thunder, birds) are cosmological analogies, not contemporary applications. Both sides remain internal.

paragraphs.core_text: These signs and these evil marks are found in the chief of the demons and fiends, the King of all the mountains of Darkness [ ... the one] to [whom] the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness and its wrath [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary statement recapitulating the King's attributes. 'The land of darkness has given birth' to the King — cosmic genesis, internal to the system. Heavy lacunae at end.

paragraphs.core_text: ... more than all his fellow rulers, who are in all his worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragment continuing from ¶10 across a lacuna. Positions the King above his fellow rulers — hierarchical cosmic statement, internal to the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Gold is the body of the King of the realms of Darkness. The body of all the powers who belong to the world of Smoke is gold. And also, the taste of its fruits is salty.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'The spirit of the King, of the realms of Darkness, is this one who reigns today in the principalities and authorities of the earth and the entire universe. I mean these who reign over the entire creation, humiliating mankind with tyranny, according to their heart's desire.' — 'reigns today in the principalities and authorities' explicitly reaches outside the cosmic system into contemporary power structures. 'I mean these who reign over' is editorial gloss language.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First of the five sub-king descriptions. The substrate maps realm→metal→taste (Smoke→gold→salty). The editorial bridge applies 'the spirit of the King' to contemporary principalities. The boundary is sharp: the mapping cosmos→cosmos stops at 'salty,' then 'The spirit of the King... reigns today' crosses into the editorial present. The editorial_bridge score (12.2) correctly flags the later material.

paragraphs.core_text: In contrast, the King of the worlds of Fire is lion-faced, the foremost of all the beasts. Copper is his body. Again, the body of all the rulers who belong to Fire is copper. Their taste is the sour taste that is in every form.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'Also, the spirit of the King, of they that belong to the world of Fire, is this one who reigns in the greater ones and the leaders; who are under the command of the principalities and authorities and the kings of the world. Also a spirit of his is found in these sects that worship fire, as their sacrifices are offered to fire.' — applies cosmic spirit to contemporary power hierarchy and identifies fire-worshipping sects. Both 'principalities and authorities' and 'sects that worship fire' reach outside the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second sub-king: Fire→lion-faced→copper→sour. The substrate portion is pristine correspondential mapping. 'In contrast' connects to the preceding systematic enumeration. The editorial extension follows the same formula as ¶12 ('the spirit of the King... is this one who reigns') and adds identification of fire-worshipping sects — unmistakably editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, the King of the worlds of Wind is eagle-face. His body is iron. Also, the body of all they who belong to the Wind is iron. Their taste is the sharp taste that is in every form.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'His spirit is the one of idolatry to the spirits of error who are in every temple, the sites of idols, the sites of statue- and image-worship, the shrines of the error of the world.' — 'every temple, the sites of idols, the sites of statue- and image-worship' are specific religious institutions in the editor's contemporary world. The syntax mimics the substrate ('His spirit is the one of...') but one side of the mapping has left the cosmic system.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third sub-king: Wind→eagle-face→iron→sharp. This paragraph is the clearest illustration of the substrate/editorial boundary: 'His body is iron' maps cosmos→cosmos; 'His spirit is the one of idolatry... in every temple' maps cosmos→contemporary religious landscape. Same syntax, different temporal layer. Editorial_bridge score (36.99) is the highest in the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: For his part, the King of the world of Water is fish-face. His body is silver. All the other rulers who belong to Water, silver is their body. Also, the taste of their fruit is the sweetness of water, the sweet taste that is in every (form).
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'Again, the spirit of the King, of the rulers of Water, is this one who reigns today in the sects of error; these that dip the baptism of the waters, (setting) their hope and their trust in the baptism of the waters.' — 'reigns today in the sects of error' and 'baptism of the waters' identify contemporary baptismal cults. 'Today' explicitly anchors to the editorial present.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth sub-king: Water→fish-face→silver→sweet. 'For his part' is a structural transitional marker connecting the systematic enumeration. The editorial extension identifies baptismal sects — likely Mandaeans or Elchasaites, contemporary to the Manichaean editors. 'Reigns today' is the signature editorial bridge formula.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [the Kin]g of the world of Darkness is a dragon. His [body is lead] and tin. All the other rulers [who belong to the world of] Darkness, their body is lead and tin. And also, the taste of their fruits is bitterness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial bridge: 'Again, the spirit who reigns in them is the spirit who speaks till today in the soothsayers, giving oracles; in the givers of portents, every type; in they who are possessed; and the other spirits that give oracles, every type.' — 'speaks till today in the soothsayers' reaches into the contemporary world of divination practitioners. 'Till today' is the editorial present-tense anchor.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth sub-king: Darkness→dragon→lead and tin→bitter. Completes the five-fold correspondence system. The editorial extension identifies contemporary soothsayers and oracle-givers. Note: the sub-world of Darkness within the broader Land of Darkness — Gardner notes the redactor's confusion about this hierarchical distinction.

Pure devotional closure: 'Concerning this I tell you, my brethren and my limbs' — direct audience address; 'the perfect faithful, the holy elect' — institutional community titles; 'Hold your heart close to you, and you stay away from' — imperative moral instruction; 'break loose their chain and their chastening for ever' — eschatological promise. Every marker of the exhortation layer is present. The 'five enslavements of the five dark spirits' and 'service of their five bodies' reference the substrate's five-fold structure but apply it pastorally — the correspondence is being USED, not BEING. High exhortation score (42.62) confirms.
